name: lentil cottage pie
instructions:
Jamie Oliver's cottage pie — the CUMIN + MARMITE line — its own recipe now (formerly 'variant C / the pub stew' of the dissolved mushroomed-lentils-british file). SERVED AS A SIDE, WITH MASHED POTATOES.

=== THE BUILD ===

- DICED ONION + MINCED GARLIC + DICED/MINCED MUSHROOMS (NOT pureed — the chunk is nice; see notes), sautéed in BUTTER — NO OLIVE OIL.
- GLUTAMATES: TOMATO PASTE + WORCESTERSHIRE SAUCE + PORCINI POWDER + MARMITE — leaning MORE ON TOMATO, LESS ON MARMITE. NO DARK STOCK (marmite + dark stock is too much MSG — see notes; tomato paste + marmite is all you need, like Jamie says).
- SEASONING: ROSEMARY + CUMIN + THYME (thyme is primary, but ROSEMARY IS MORE CRITICAL). CARAWAY IS CLASHING (fits the pickle-relish stew, turns horrible overnight here). If rosemary is unavailable, BAY LEAF is the most appropriate substitute.
- ACID: a RELATIVELY GENEROUS amount of LEMON JUICE to balance.
- LENTILS: BROWN / SPANISH lentils.
- POTATOES: AS MASH, UNDERNEATH — the stew is served ON TOP of mashed potatoes, not with diced potato inside. The potatoes need to be there; mash is where they live. CELERIAC, TURNIPS, SWEDE/RUTABAGA secondary — they're in the Jamie Oliver. CARROTS and CELERY are CLASHING.
- RED CHILI FLAKES (secondary).

THE FLAVOR ENGINE: CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON JUICE — LEMON balances the ROSEMARY and the MARMITE; CUMIN balances the LEMON.

SERVE: ON TOP OF MASHED POTATOES.

BALANCE WARNING: sensitive to TOO MUCH FLAVOR INJECTOR OF ANY KIND — rosemary, marmite, and lemon all overshoot easily. Hard to balance; respect the engine.
notes:
Split out 2026-10-31 from the dissolved mushroomed-lentils-british file: this is the JAMIE OLIVER cottage pie line (cumin + marmite), its own recipe, served as a side with mashed potatoes. (Nisha Vora's lentil wellington, which shared that file, was removed — not interested in making it.)

=== THE GLUTAMATE STACK: TOMATO + MARMITE, NO DARK STOCK ===

THE MAJOR BALANCE PROBLEM, found: MARMITE + DARK VEGETABLE STOCK is just TOO MUCH MSG. You only need TOMATO PASTE and MARMITE, like Jamie Oliver says (his Allotment Cottage Pie runs on the blended porcini/marmite/tomato-paste paste, no stock, no roux). Lean MORE ON TOMATO and LESS ON MARMITE. PORCINI POWDER adds glutamates WITHOUT tipping the scales. WORCESTERSHIRE is a GREAT addition, frankly — primary in the stack. Butter only for the sauté — no olive oil. (The no-marmite path — dark stock as the anchor instead — became its own recipe: [[shittake-lentil-soup]].)

=== THE FLAVOR ENGINE: CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON ===

CUMIN + ROSEMARY + LEMON JUICE is a FLAVOR ENGINE and they all play well together: LEMON balances the ROSEMARY and the MARMITE, while CUMIN balances the LEMON. Use a relatively generous amount of lemon juice. If rosemary is unavailable, BAY LEAF is the most appropriate substitute. THYME is good and PRIMARY — but ROSEMARY IS MORE CRITICAL.

MARMITE'S BUFFERS: marmite works here because rosemary/thyme and the potato back it up — the buffers absorb its intensity. The sparer [[mushroom-pickle-relish]] stew lacks those buffers and prefers DARK ALE in its anchor slot.

=== CARAWAY IS CLASHING; CUMIN IS NECESSARY (THE LEFTOVERS TEST) ===

CARAWAY IS WRONG HERE — it fits [[mushroom-pickle-relish]], but it's CLASHING in this recipe. It tasted OK in the pot, but OVERNIGHT IT JUST TURNED HORRIBLE — judge a stew by its leftover state, not its day-one state. CUMIN, on the other hand, is NECESSARY — a third of the flavor engine.

=== MINCED MUSHROOMS, NOT PUREED ===

MINCING the mushrooms instead of pureeing is better here — the CHUNK is nice in the final product, because this recipe LACKS VEGETABLES and it's a substantial dish, not a gravy. (A break from the pureed-mushroom gravy engine of [[creamy-french-lentils]].)

=== POTATOES — MASH UNDERNEATH, NOT DICED INSIDE ===

The potatoes NEED to be there, but this dish is better serviced ON TOP OF MASHED POTATOES — not with diced potato inside the stew. (The mushrooms/herbs/lentils still want the potato — it just lives under the stew as mash.) Presumably RED CHILI FLAKES are good. CELERIAC, TURNIPS, SWEDE/RUTABAGA are secondary — might have misjudged them, frankly, because they're in the Jamie Oliver (the Allotment scaffold runs on swede + celeriac). CARROTS and CELERY stay CLASHING.

=== SERVING — ON TOP OF MASHED POTATOES; PAIRINGS ===

Served ON TOP OF MASHED POTATOES (the cottage-pie lineage, inverted — Jamie's original bakes the mash on top; here the stew rides over the mash). Pairs well with RICE and with PORK — less so with CHICKEN or HOT DOGS.

=== HARDEST TO BALANCE ===

Sensitive to too much flavor injector of any kind — rosemary, marmite, lemon all overshoot easily. The biggest single culprit was stacking MARMITE + DARK STOCK; with the stock out and the engine balanced, it's much more nail-down-able.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[shittake-lentil-soup]]: the no-marmite sibling — dark stock + tomato backbone, shiitake, clean build.
- [[mushroom-pickle-relish]]: the ale + pickle + cumin/caraway stew.
- [[creamy-french-lentils]]: the mustard + cream + potato stew.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of the dark register.
original_chef: Jamie Oliver — Allotment Cottage Pie (Jamie's Veg, via The Happy Foodie); this is the cumin + marmite line of that scaffold.
